measurement_method: Registered original binary STL vertices and plane intersections. X=66.15 exposes runner support teeth; Y=169 cuts between teeth and Y=170 cuts through a tooth. Rear sections use Y=3.8 and X=0 / X=10.4. All dimensions below are in registered model coordinates, not the construction datum.

original_runner_support.symmetry: Opposed sheets at positive and negative X; listed X dimensions describe the positive side.

teeth.description: Narrow repeated connections cross the lower and upper gaps, carrying the thin sheet from the lower lip and supporting the upper lip. These were omitted by the earlier native reconstruction.
teeth.note: Original upper/lower intervals differ slightly and original tooth spacing is irregular. End connections are separate from the listed interior lower-tooth intervals.

channel_behind_sheet.description: A void remains behind the sacrificial sheet; it is not a solid runner filling.

original_rear_support.description: A thin central sheet joins two narrow vertical pillars. Pillars contact the slot floor and flare in Y to carry the full depth of its roof. The central sheet has clearance from the floor and roof between pillars.

deliberate_regularization: Runner teeth use equal 9.091176 mm pitch and 0.7 mm width rather than the source irregular intervals.
Runner sheet horizontal dimensions round the measured body limits to Y31.0..186.25 and X65.9..66.4; no long end anchor blocks remain.
Runner teeth span Z17.9..29.1 so they overlap both existing simplified planar channel lips. Existing source lip blends remain simplified.
Rear panel and pillar dimensions round source measurements to 0.01 mm and omit tiny edge transitions.
Rear pillars overlap the slot floor and roof by 0.1 mm to ensure volumetric union with the tray.

independent_review.result: Section overlay confirms original support strategy, matching sheet locations and rear pillar flare. Runner tooth positions differ deliberately; original lip blends remain simplified. No additional geometry issue identified.

removal_intent: Sacrificial print-in-place sheets and their teeth/pillars are intended to be removed after printing to clear the two runner channels and rear opening. They are not functional springs.
validation_limits: Geometry and topology were checked digitally. Physical printing, bridging, support removal, material selection and slicer settings have not been tested.
The source STL has float32 coordinate quantization; measurements are not manufacturing tolerances.
Comparison is scoped to these supports. It does not claim complete geometric identity to the purchased source.
